newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat turns up on USDA's cut in ending stocks.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat turns up on USDA's cut in ending stocks.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures rebounded from early lows, underpinned by USDA's cut in its forecast for 1996-97 U.S. ending stocks of wheat, traders said.
USDA Friday said the supply of wheat in the United States at the end of the 1996-97 crop year would total 470 million bushels, below the previous forecast for 506 million.
Wheat was pressured early by a sharp drop in corn and soybeans linked to USDA's projections for greater-than-expected supplies of those commodities.
At 1010 CDT, wheat was 1/2 to one cent per bushel higher, with December up 1/2 at $4.24-1/2.
